preamble: Prothetic [v] before word-initial back rounded vowels is a recurrent Slavic development. Belarusian inserted [v] before inherited initial *o and *u (Proto-Slavic *oko 'eye' > вока, *uxo 'ear' > вуха), and colloquial Common Czech adds v- to most words beginning with o- (vokno for standard okno 'window'). The prothetic consonant blocks a vowel-initial onset, the labial glide having strengthened to a labiodental fricative.

examples.note: Prothetic [v] before initial stressed o; compare Russian око without prothesis.
Same prothesis before initial u; compare Russian ухо.

examples.from: standard otevřít okno 'to open the window'
examples.note: Common Czech, the colloquial interdialect of Bohemia, adds prothetic v- to most o-initial words.
